(documented, by name only) Named as father of Izrael in Klimontow death act 40/1867:
"syn Rywena i Lacy". No act of his own located. Birth year estimated from his son's age.
The surname Rywen-bajrych is built on this given name.

** MY OWN ERROR, MADE AND CORRECTED 5 Aug 2026 - LEFT VISIBLE. ** I read Klimontow
marriage act 4/1834 as making Jeremiasz "urodzonym tu w Klimontowie z RYWENA y Laji" and
on that basis upgraded this couple to documented, gave them the trade of bakalarstwo, and
entered Jeremiasz as Izrael's brother. Then I read the ALEGAT to the same act - an Akt
Znania sworn before the mayor of Klimontow eight days earlier - which states at length
and unambiguously that Jeremiasz's father is HERCYK Rywenbayrych, bakalarz. At maximum
magnification the register word is NOT securely legible to me either way. A purpose-built
identity document outweighs my uncertain reading of a register line, so Jeremiasz is
entered under Hercyk the bakalarz (@I54@) and THIS COUPLE REVERTS TO PROBABLE, resting
on the 1867 act alone as before.
(inference, not confirmed) Klimontow death act 53/1835, "Laja Rywenbayrych" - act not read.

(documented, by name only) Named as mother of Izrael in Klimontow death act 40/1867.
Polish "Laca" - probably Lea or Laja.
NOTE A COINCIDENCE WORTH WATCHING: marriage act 4/1834 gives Jeremiasz's mother as "Laji",
and Jeremiasz's father is Hercyk, not Rywen. So either there were two couples in this town
with a wife called Laja/Laca, or the two men are more closely tangled than I can yet see.
Do not merge them on the strength of the shared given name.

"urodzonym tu w Klimontowie", and aged fourteen in August 1834. I could not read the age

NO BIRTH RECORD EXISTS: the Akt Znania was drawn up precisely because he could not
produce one, "z powodu nie utrzymywania dawniey Ksiag Metrykalnych" - the Klimontow
Jewish registers do not reach back before about 1826.

MAIDEN NAME UNRESOLVED, and I am recording this as a limit of my own reading rather
than pretending to a conclusion. Across seven birth acts read in the original, the
maiden-name formula reads: 46/1845 "z Leml(ow)"; 12/1847 illegible; 27/1854
"z Lemkowiczow"; 20/1856 "z Kimetow"; 25/1858 no maiden name given; 12/1861
"z Komkowiczow"; 19/1863 "z Lemkowiczow" (the clearest of them); 52/1865 "z Lemelow";
42/1867 "z Lemkowiczow". Two live candidates: LEMKOWICZ / LEMEL (five readings, and
the clearest single one), or KIMET - and the 1856 act is witnessed by Ejzyk Kimet, the
synagogue beadle, which is what a bride's kinsman would be doing there. A Kimet/Kimel
family is demonstrably present in Klimontow and witnesses these acts repeatedly.
I twice adopted a reading here and twice had to reverse it. It stays open.

CAUTION - competing identification. This man's name and birth year match the Page of
Testimony's "Tuvia, b. 1888" for Chana's FATHER almost exactly, which raised the
possibility that Chana's father was a Wajsblum and her mother a Rywenbajrych - the
reverse of what the Pages say. Weighing against that: the Pages name the mother
"Bajla-Szajndla", and that distinctive double name occurs exactly once in all 517
Wajsblum records of Radom Gubernia - the 1892 Opatow birth (@I24@). A common male given
name matching is much weaker evidence than a rare double female name matching. See
findings/008 for the full argument, including the unexplained fact that Opatow's
9,135 indexed records contain not one Rywenbajrych.
** SUPERSEDED IN PART, 14 Aug 2026: @I24@ is no longer held to be a child of this
family (see @F60@), so this man is no longer entered as HER brother - he remains a
son of Moszek and Gella by the birth-sequence argument alone. The 008 identification
question above is unaffected: he is still not Chana's father. **
** 14 Aug 2026, later: his marriage is now on record - Stopnica, act 25/1909, to Liba
Rozenman (@F62@, @S83@). That index row names his parents outright, "Moszek WAJSBLUM,
Gela GINSBURG", so this man's place in @F10@ no longer rests on the birth-sequence
argument alone; what remains inferred is only the equation of the 1909 groom (aged 20,
b. Opatow) with birth act 88/1889 - a match of year, town and name. The row also adds
weight against the 008 identification: a man who married a Rozenman in Stopnica in
1909 is a poorer fit for Chana's father, though not an impossible one (remarriage). **

PLACE UNLOCATED, and this is the principal open question on this side. Two documented
negatives: (1) he was not born in Klimontow between 1826 and 1892 - the JRI index covers

off the film, 183 entries in all, each list closed by its own protocol, with nothing in
the R section; (2) Opatow's 9,135 indexed records, covering births, marriages and deaths
to 1917, contain not one Rywenbajrych. Two further negatives since: Arolsen returns
nothing on the surname in any spelling (control Kestenbaum = 587), and FamilySearch's
indexed records contain no Rywenbajrych at all worldwide on an exact search (control
Wajsblum = 56) - though FamilySearch holds no Polish vital registers, so that zero is
weak. LEAD CLOSED: Yad Vashem 4631872/4631873 "Rywenbeirech, Tobiasch, b. 20.07.1888,
Lodz" is a DIFFERENT MAN - a permanent resident of Lodz, Steinmetzgasse 25 apt. 18, from
the "Lodz Names" volume. Ours is a permanent resident of Opatow. Same name and year;
probably kin, but not him. Do not chase Lodz for Tuvia's birthplace. See findings/011.

** Survived the Shoah, and is now documented in a wartime record: CHANA RYWENBAJRYCH
appears on the lists of Jewish inmates at Skarzysko-Kamienna designated "sick",
November 1942 - February 1943. This is the first time she appears in a document made
at the time rather than in testimony given afterwards. **
It also puts the family story on a documentary footing from both sides: Chaim is
recorded at Skarzysko in 1942 on CKZP slip 12344, and Chana is now recorded there too.
They said they met in a camp; the records place them both in the same camp.

(documented) The Arolsen tracing-file index of 1947 carries her as "Chana Albert
[Sara], maiden name Rywenbeirich, b. 18 Jun 1917" - case 705604, consecutive with
her husband's 705603, i.e. one joint request (findings/066). This corroborates the
18.06.1917 birth date of the 2015 citizenship application from a record made
sixty-eight years earlier, and carries the same "Sara" that stands on her Holon
gravestone and in the Opatow municipal index ("Chana-Sara").

Shot. Chana's younger sister - it was Amotz's memory of this murdered sister that
opened the whole Opatow line.
CONFLICT, RESOLVED IN THE FAMILY'S FAVOUR: the 1988 Opatow memorial list places her
at Treblinka on 23 October 1942 with her parents. But a contemporaneous German camp
document - the lists of Skarzysko-Kamienna inmates designated "sick", November 1942
to February 1943 - carries a FAJGA RYWENBAJRYCH, i.e. alive and in the camp AFTER
that date. A record made at the time outweighs a list compiled by survivors in 1988,
whose compilers evidently assumed the whole household died in the October deportation.
At Skarzysko the "sick" designation was in practice a selection list.
The family's account was right.

(documented) A fifth Page of Testimony for her surfaced 14 Aug 2026: item 394902,
filled in by her great-uncle MOSHE Wajsblum on 26 June 1957 as sheet 13146-1 - the
FIRST sheet of the same envelope as his Pages for Bejla, Reizel and the two husbands.
He wrote her as "Feiga BEIRACH", his usual shorthand for Rywenbajrych, father Tuvia,
mother Bila, born Opatow, single; field 11 reads only "extermination" (hashmada) -
no place, no date - and fields for birth year and children are blank. The only Page
for her by someone of her parents' generation. It adds no date and does not disturb
the Skarzysko resolution above.

"Brother-in-law"). His self-declared relations are the backbone of family @F60@.

by Amotz; the signing line reads "T.A., 5717"). Birth and death dates unknown; not
known to be living, so entered without further personal data. Descendants, if any,
are the most direct living line to this branch. Distinguish him from the OTHER
Moshe Veisblum in Yad Vashem's submitter index, a Radom survivor who filed some
forty Pages for Radom, Kielce and Suchedniow families (findings/057 par. 3).

(documented) After liberation, recovered 15 Aug 2026 (findings/088). By 1947 he was
living in KREIS SCHWABMUENCHEN, Bavaria, registered on an Arolsen F18 list of
"55 Jews who were living in Kreis Schwabmuenchen in 1947" (ref 8806110) - entry 50,
"Weisblum Alter, 24.10.03, Opatow, last residence Starachowice", with his wife Hela
immediately below him at entry 51. ** Entries 52 and 53 on that same page are Hena
and Chaja Weisblum of Opatow, the daughters of Chil and Sura (findings/087) - four
Wajsblums from Opatow among 55 people in one Bavarian district. Suggestive of kin
who regrouped; it is a residence list, not a family list, and proves no relation. **
He left Bremen on 25 Jun 1948 from the Bremen-Grohn resettlement camp, by air
("Flug Nr. 3"), aged 44, married, occupation millworker, arriving Prestwich (a

** OVERSTATED, CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR — read this whole note. ** I first wrote that the
2015 application "resolves" the date. It does not, and I should not have said so. The date
11.07.1907 already existed on a CKZP registration card in our own hands; the 1913 came from
CKZP slip 12344. Both are POST-WAR SELF-DECLARATIONS of the same class. The 2015 filing
simply repeats one of the two - so it tells us **which date the family committed to**, and
is NOT an independent source for the year. The conflict is therefore NOT resolved by
evidence; it is resolved only as a matter of which the family used.
** 1907 is adopted here** because it is the date the family put before a state authority,
and because it is a specific day-month-year rather than a bare year - but it stays ONE
post-war declaration against another.

The family's
own official Polish citizenship application of 2015 (12-page WNIOSEK to the Wojewoda
Mazowiecki) gives him, in a structured field, as born **11 / 07 / 1907**.
The competing "1913" came from CKZP slip 12344 ("ur. 1913 W-wa"); a second CKZP card had
already given 11.07.1907 and I had left the conflict open. The 2015 filing settles it in
favour of 1907 - a date the family committed to in a state document.
** CONSEQUENCE: my whole Warsaw birth-register search ran on the wrong year. ** I read the
1913 alphabetical index of cyrkul VI (unit 72/200/0/-/110, scans 110-114, sections А and
Э) and found no Alpert/Albert/Elbert. That negative stands but is irrelevant - it is for
a year that is not his. So I redid it on 1907 - and:
** NO 1907 WARSAW JEWISH BIRTH REGISTER SURVIVES IN FOND 72/200/0 AT ALL. ** For 1907 the
fond holds only marriages (cyrkul IV = -/66, 151 scans; cyrkul V = -/98, 152 scans) and two
unscanned marriage-annex units (-/251, -/252). There are combined birth/marriage/death
units for 1906, 1908 and 1909, but none for 1907.
** And JRI's Warsaw birth index has no Alpert/Albert/Elbert birth with a mother RUDLA, and
none named Chaim in 1907. ** Indexed Warsaw Alpert/Albert births run 1871-1905 with nothing
after Jakow Josif 1905.
** CONCLUSION: on both candidate years the register is gone. Chaim's Warsaw birth act very
probably does not survive. ** What remains: another Warsaw fond or duplicate series
(unchecked), and asking Daniela Regev what document 11.07.1907 was taken from.
The gravestone says only "born Warsaw", which is consistent with either year.

Ester Gitla's - the mother is consistently "Ryfka". From 1855 the registers write
